7. Reproduce shard 3/8: `cd e2e && node scripts/shard-specs.mjs 3 8` (expect `02,14,20,33,41,47`), then `pnpm exec cypress run --browser chrome --spec "<that comma list>"`. ## Tests

- Fuzz single-seed replays (no new test file; the gate is the test): `cargo jackioh fuzz --from <seed> --seeds 1` (plus `--handicap` / `--duos` variants) — asserts no-throw, real `state.result`, replay hash equality, invariants, growth, probes. Must print the pass summary with zero failures.
- Fuzz regression guard: if the seed's decks are pool-shift-sensitive, pin them under `crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/` following `crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/README.md` and run `cargo jackioh fuzz --regress`; plus `cargo test -p jackioh-tools fuzz` (seeds 1–20 smoke wave, `SWEEP_SEEDS`).
- Card test in the touched script file, named after the card's existing convention in that file's `mod tests` (and after the ruling, e.g. `fn r2500xxx_<what>` if step 9 applied): asserts the corrected effect sequence for the failing board. Run `cargo test -p jackioh-cards <card_id>`.
- Engine test only if step 5 touched the engine: the new test lives in the touched module's tests, named `fn r2500xxx_<what>` when a ruling exists, asserting the corrected read-helper/effect behavior. Run `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --test 'rules*' r2500xxx`.
- E2E specs, each by file: `pnpm --dir e2e exec cypress run --browser chrome --spec cypress/e2e/<failing-spec>.cy.ts` for every spec changed, passing clean (not tolerated-flaky). E2E house rules hold: seeded, no `cy.wait(ms)`.
- Web unit test only if a client file changed: `pnpm --dir apps/web test <touched-test-file>` (builds WASM first via `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh`).
- Checks: `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy -p <touched-crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo jackioh catalog check`; `cargo jackioh patches check`; `cargo jackioh spec check` when a ruling was added or an R-id cited.

## Done when

- [ ] `fuzz (3/4)` root-caused to a seed/wave/stage and fixed; single-seed replay passes and the shard wave passes.
- [ ] `e2e (3/8)`, `(5/8)`, `(6/8)` each root-caused to a spec/test and fixed robustly; each touched spec passes; no test skipped, disabled, quarantined, or re-run into green.
- [ ] Every added test fails without the fix (checked by stashing the fix, or stated how).
- [ ] All commands under Tests and Checks above pass for what changed.
- [ ] PR body says per job which fix makes it pass and how it was checked; any `.github/` remainder is exact lines for a person.
- [ ] No file outside Files to touch changed; `git status` shows only intended files.

## Risks

- Determinism/replay: fuzz games derive decks, game, and policy from `Rng::new` seed strings; a fix that reads the clock, OS randomness, hash order, or thread state breaks replay equality. Keep all game input in `(seed, decks, log)` and verify with the replay assertion.
- Hidden information: e2e/client fixes must go through intent + `view_for`; the AI and probes never see hidden cards (`I6`). A client or test that asserts on hidden state leaks it — assert on the player view only.
- Growth/settle caps: a card fix that emits more events per action can trip `GROWTH_*_BOUND` or the §10.3 settle cap on other seeds; the full shard-3 wave (step 3) guards this, not just the single seed.
- R144 reseed: networked specs (05, 09, 20, 41, 42 among the failed shards) share fixture accounts/invite codes; each shard boots a fresh server — never "fix" by ordering specs or reusing spent codes.
- Chrome-under-Cypress flakiness (`e2e/README.md`: Chrome 155 network-service drops) looks like product failure; check `client.log`/`server.log` and the failure signature before changing product code, and route any pin change through the person-owned `.github/` note, not a local workaround.

## Open questions

- None blocks the builder: all reproduction uses the job's own commands on this branch. If a failure no longer reproduces here (the branch sits five commits past `0e5ae82`), say which job, on what evidence (shard wave output), and fix only what still fails. If any remainder lives solely in `.github/` (workflow, action, schedule, pin), the builder cannot change it: put the exact lines in the PR body and ask a person.
